title: Minimax Recruitment Design for Cluster-Level Treatment Interactions with Rare Recruitment Cells
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Math and decision panels pass, six citations verified-attested; paper score ceiling6.1<7.4.
gap_reasons: The contribution is a specialized decision-theoretic composition rather than a broadly reusable methodology.
Both executed examples have g=0 and uniquely select m=1, leaving the substantive recruitment trade-off with positive cluster variance unevaluated.
The moderate-noise transfer beginning at B=10^8 provides limited operational evidence for the prospective design application.
Narrow scope and limited demonstrated recruitment consequences constrain the projected journal score.
The final Honest scope section incorrectly describes supplied proofs and computations as deferred, creating contradictory completion claims that faithful writing must reconcile.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived the full original-budget common-parameter minimax limit, balanced-label assignment and a rational risk certifier; both informal math and decision panels passed, all six sources verified-attested. Main replayed 104000 balanced and 368000 complete-randomization dual inequalities and 1001 parameter points each; both risk brackets have width below .001 and exclude every m>=2. The result was banked incremental below the unchanged field floor (score6.1<7.4); no F stages, Lean certification, promotion, presentation or git commit, and the stale Honest scope wording remains disclosed.
tldr: A prespecified cluster-level treatment interaction can retain finite random support even when a trial budget grows. The Gaussian recruitment benchmark evaluates the original-budget optimum over every legal recruitment integer, label-conditioned exact-half assignment kernel and original-record estimator. Finite nuisance reduction and conditional experiment ordering lead to a Poisson-count Gaussian decision value with one common interaction prior. A proved and implemented rational certifier chooses recruitment, reconstructs a nuisance-valid original-data rule and certifies it against every admissible competitor. At the moderate-noise input \((\Lambda,c,s,g,e,H)=(4,1,1,0,1/10,1)\), independently checked common-prior certificates uniquely choose \(m=1\), prove a limiting gain of at least \(0.188818825571\) over complete randomization with its best estimator, and transfer uniformly to every integer budget \(B\ge10^8\). The contribution is an incremental technical composition of credited decision and design tools.
gap: Ryan, Esserman and Li evaluate interaction variance under cluster and individual recruitment costs. Critical rare recruitment creates missing-cell events that a variance criterion does not price. Existing bounded-normal-mean computations address the scalar decision machinery, while the inspected constrained-design results do not settle the full original-budget common-interaction game.
fill: Exact finite nuisance reduction, allocation dominance and an all-integer tail certificate connect recruitment to one jointly optimized random-count risk. The open rational certifier returns a purchase, treatment allocation and original-record decision rule whose risk is certified against every admissible competitor.
